nodes.answer: The IPAs program employs a bottom-up approach that involves national and regional stakeholders and promotes community-led management.

Global agreements have recognized the significance of these plants and have since prioritized them in global targets. In particular, the CBD Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiver - sity Framework (GBF) targets 9, 10, 11 and 13 emphasize nature S contribution to humans, with aims to restore and enhance nature S benefits, use species sustainably and encourage the utili- zation of knowledge and practices of Indigenous Peoples and local communities. A valuable area-based conservation tool directly aligning with these targets is the Impor - tant Plant Areas (IPAs) framework. IPAs are defined as the most important places in the world for wild plant and fungal diversity that can be protected and managed as specific sites. IPAs are identified using a criteria-based assessment of threatened species, botanical richness and threat- ened habitats (Darbyshire et al. 2017; Plantlife 2018). nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: In what context was the participatory MCA methodology validated?
nodes.answer: It was validated during an all-day workshop on Tinos, a Greek island on the Aegean Sea.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Climate change challenges necessitate innovative, effective and sustainable mitigation measures to enhance ecosystem resilience. This study presents the development and ap - plication of a participatory, and cross-sectoral multi-criteria assessment (MCA) decision- support tool designed to prioritize Nature-based Solutions (NBS) and Bioeconomy Solu - tions (BES) based on Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem (WEFE) nexus and selected impact (Social, Economic, Climate change, Institutional) criteria. The methodology and tool are adaptable in different contexts and can address several climate change, sustainability, and circularity challenges. The participatory MCA methodology was applied and validated during an all-day workshop on Tinos, a Greek island on the Aegean Sea. Local challenges were addressed and examined within the framework of two distinct sites. Workshop results identified habitat loss and biodiversity decline as the island S primary challenges, with Conservation Agriculture and Agroforestry emerging as the top-rated solutions, scoring 78/100 and 71/100, respectively. Although stakeholders prioritized different interventions for each site, the selected solutions consistently aimed to address these environmental issues. This research study contributes to advancing understanding and practice in the field of sustainable resource management within the WEFE nexus, while underscoring the importance of participatory approaches in developing effective and context-specific sustainability strategies.

nodes.question: Who are the contributors mentioned as part of creating a Nature-Positive World?
nodes.answer: Contributors to creating a Nature-Positive World include Locke, Rockström, Bakker, Bapna, and others involved in biodiversity initiatives.
